kind: The shared sub-tabs component (layout budget test L-03), landed on its own so the customer and public tracks can reuse it. No page uses it in this change.
findingsNote: No GAP id is created or changed.
sensitive: no: a presentation component with no page using it. It reads the address and the page, and holds no session, role or token code.
changed: apps/web/components/ux/sub-tabs.tsx and sub-tabs.css: SubTabs, SubTab and revealInSubTabs
apps/web/lib/ux/sub-tabs.ts: resolveSubTab, nextTabIndex, withTab, safeDecode (pure, tested without a browser)
tests/integration/ux-sub-tabs.test.ts (16 tests) and tests/ux/sub-tabs.spec.ts (11 tests, the L-03 reference)
behaviour: A labelled tablist of tabs, each owning one panel; automatic activation; only the chosen tab is in the tab order.
The chosen tab is kept in ?tab= and other words in the address are kept; nothing loads.
An old #id lands: a tab id, an alias, a panel anchor or any element inside a panel opens its tab and the element is scrolled to and focused. The old #id wins over ?tab=.
A hash that points outside the tabs is left alone (the team workspace uses the hash to name the section being shown).
Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs and wrap; the arrows mirror in a right-to-left page.
Every panel stays in the server HTML, hidden unless chosen, so entries survive a switch and no content is lost.
Tabs are 44 px, wrap on a phone and never scroll the page sideways; axe finds nothing on any tab, left to right and right to left.
revealInSubTabs(element) opens the tab that holds an element so a Jump to control can land on a heading.
A hash that cannot be decoded (such as %E0%A4%A) names nothing: the first tab is shown and no page error is raised (safeDecode is used everywhere the hash is read).
Callers own the five-tab cap of the layout budget; the component shows every tab it is given.
